problem_statement: The preetsuthar17/discord-bot-website-template project is a small Next.js pages-router Discord bot website with a landing page, a /commands page, a shared dark frosted-glass card system, CTA buttons, a bot online status asset, and CSS accordion command groups. Add a new cross-page Automations browser: a dedicated /automations page built from the site's shared card/section pattern that surfaces six ready-to-run automation presets grouped into categories, with a category filter tab row and a live result readout so a visitor can narrow the presets by category. Register Automations in a shared cross-page navigation so the same nav link renders on the landing page and the new Automations page. Preserve the original hero, About cards, Join now CTA, footer links, command accordion behavior, dark dotted background, Next.js build, and responsive layout.
required_content: Keep the Next.js pages-router build, / landing route, /commands route, shared Navbar, Footer, Showcase, About, JoinNow components, command accordion radio inputs, source-code link, bot online status asset, and dark dotted background intact.
Add a new /automations page rendered from the shared frosted-glass card pattern with a heading titled exactly Automations.

The Automations page must present six automation preset cards titled exactly Welcome New Members, Auto Moderation Filters, Scheduled Announcements, Reaction Role Menus, Ticket Support Threads, and Level and XP Rewards, each an h3 card title with a glyph image, a category label, and a description.

Add a category filter tab row above the preset grid with All, Onboarding, Moderation, and Engagement tabs, and a live readout that reports how many presets are shown in the format Showing N of 6 followed by the active category, for example Showing 6 of 6 for All presets. Assign each preset to a category: Welcome New Members and Reaction Role Menus are Onboarding; Auto Moderation Filters and Ticket Support Threads are Moderation; Scheduled Announcements and Level and XP Rewards are Engagement (so Moderation has 2 of 6). Clicking a category tab must filter the grid to that category and update the readout count and label, for example clicking Moderation shows Showing 2 of 6.

Introduce a shared cross-page navigation registry rendered as anchors carrying the nav-link class, and register Automations in it so the same Automations nav link renders on both the landing page and the Automations page.
The shared navigation must also keep Home, Commands, and the existing GitHub source link reachable without replacing the original Navbar or Footer.

Keep the change dependency-free and localized to a shared nav registry/component, a shared card component, a filter-enabled page, a style partial, and _app import; do not replace the command accordion with a static image.
Preserve accordion interactions for the Utilities and Fun command groups after the new Automations section is added.
design_constraints: Keep the original dark background, frosted cards, white/gray typography, 5px radius, compact button styling, BOT brand, and command accordion visual rhythm recognizable; the Automations cards must reuse the same card system.
Do not add backend APIs, external status widgets, analytics scripts, Discord OAuth, or new dependencies.
Do not remove placeholder command rows; this task measures cross-page design-system consistency and an in-page category filter, not command copy repair.
The category filter tab row, the readout, and the Automations cards must wrap cleanly on tablet and mobile without horizontal overflow, and the preset cards must remain legible and non-overlapping.
Keep source changes small: one shared nav registry, one shared nav component, one shared card component, one filter-enabled page, one style partial, and the _app import.
state_constraints: desktop_home and mobile_home protect the original landing page hero, BOT brand, CTA buttons, about stats, bot online copy, and responsive shell while confirming the shared Automations nav link renders cross-page.
tablet_home confirms the shared navigation wraps cleanly at tablet width and still exposes the Automations nav link.

desktop_automations verifies the new Automations page renders the six shared preset cards, the Automations heading, the category filter tab row, the readout, the shared navigation, and the footer without overlap or contrast failure.
mobile_automations and tablet_automations verify the category filter row and the Automations card grid wrap without horizontal overflow on small and mid viewports.
automations_filter clicks the Moderation category tab and verifies the grid filters to that category and the live readout updates its count and label.

change_completion: A new /automations page renders six shared preset cards (Welcome New Members through Level and XP Rewards) built from the site's card system.
Automations is registered in a shared cross-page navigation so the nav-link renders on both the landing page and the Automations page.
regression: The original hero, About cards, Join now CTA, footer, BOT brand, bot online status, source link, and /commands navigation remain intact.
Utilities and Fun accordion groups still open on desktop/mobile after the Automations section is added.
design_consistency: The Automations cards match the existing dark glass card system, typography, button radius, border treatment, and compact spacing.
The Automations section is visually additive and does not dominate or replace the original landing hierarchy.
responsive: Automations cards and the shared navigation wrap without horizontal overflow on tablet and mobile.
The original navbar/footer wrapping remains usable on mobile.
state_coverage: Captured states cover the landing page and the new Automations page across desktop, tablet, and mobile with the cross-page shared navigation.

metadata.design_goal: extend an existing site with a new cross-page section while preserving the local visual language and unrelated page behavior
metadata.source_repo_kind: Small Next.js pages-router Discord bot website with landing page, commands route, shared navbar/footer, image asset, and CSS accordion command groups
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Unused runnable AI/bot web UI candidate that builds cleanly and naturally supports a cross-page consistency-add task: a shared frosted-glass card system and a two-page structure make a new nav-registered Automations section measurable across pages without external API keys.

author_notes: Slot slot_277 targets ai_chat_app / design_continuity / add / cross_page / L3 as a Consistency task. It adds a new /automations page built from the shared card/section pattern and registers Automations in a manufactured shared cross-page navigation (nav-link class) so the same nav link renders on the landing page and the Automations page, while preserving the hero, About cards, footer, image asset, and command accordion behavior.
